parts.title: Part 1
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Where does the man think he left his wallet?
questions.explanation: He remembers putting his wallet down in the waiting room before rushing to catch his next train. He still had it when he bought food at the shop.
questions.evidence: Afterwards I went to sit in the waiting room. I remember putting my wallet down.

questions.prompt: What is tomorrow’s talk at the Nature Society about?
questions.explanation: Tomorrow’s talk concerns wild flowers in parks and gardens. Rivers were the previous topic, and rainforests will be covered next month.
questions.evidence: This one’ll deal with something closer to home — wild flowers in parks and gardens.

questions.prompt: What will the woman order for lunch?
questions.explanation: Her usual lunch is salad. After learning that every lunchtime dish includes fresh bread, she chooses her usual meal, so she orders the salad.
questions.evidence: In that case, I’ll go for my usual choice.
questions.cueStartQuote: You normally have salad for lunch, don’t you?
questions.cueEndQuote: In that case, I’ll go for my usual choice.

questions.prompt: How did the woman find out about the exhibition?
questions.explanation: She heard about the exhibition on the radio. She had not seen it advertised on the gallery’s website or on posters around town.
questions.evidence: according to what I heard on the radio, it’s only on for a couple of days

questions.prompt: What is the woman’s brother doing?
questions.explanation: Her brother wanted to be a shop assistant, but the shop needed a security guard and gave him that job instead.
questions.evidence: they only needed a security guard for the shop. So he was given that job instead.

questions.prompt: How will the woman travel to her meeting?
questions.explanation: Her train has been cancelled and the taxi queue is too long. She decides it will be quicker to go home and get her own car.
questions.evidence: It’ll be quicker to rush home and get my own car rather than wait for a taxi.

questions.prompt: Which sport has the man stopped doing?
questions.explanation: He says ice hockey was too fast and he gave it up. He still enjoys both snowboarding and skiing.
questions.evidence: Ice-hockey too — I’ve always enjoyed watching it. It’s too fast, though, and I gave it up in the end.

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: You will hear two people talking about buying a bicycle. The woman suggests that the man should
questions.explanation: She suggests speaking to her brother, who is a professional cyclist. He can give useful, independent advice, so she recommends consulting an expert.
questions.evidence: What about talking to my brother who’s a professional cyclist? He’d give you some useful ideas

questions.prompt: You will hear a man telling his friend about his Welsh language course. What does the man say about it?
questions.explanation: His main difficulty is the speed at which the teacher speaks. The grammar is easier than expected, and he feels the one-hour lessons end too soon.
questions.evidence: if she spoke more slowly, I’d understand a lot more. I miss so much.

questions.prompt: You will hear a woman telling her colleague about her weekend. What did the woman like about it?
questions.explanation: The wet trip to the market was unpleasant, but sitting on the sofa watching television the next day gave her a much-needed rest.
questions.evidence: we just sat on the sofa watching TV all afternoon, which was something I really needed to do

questions.prompt: You will hear two friends talking about a new restaurant. They both think the restaurant would be better if
questions.explanation: The woman says the food seemed tinned or frozen, and the man agrees with her. They think fresher food would improve the restaurant.
questions.evidence: everything seemed to either be out of a tin or frozen.
questions.cueEndQuote: Such a shame, but you’re absolutely right

questions.prompt: You will hear two old friends talking at a party. How is the man’s appearance different from before?
questions.explanation: The man says he is still getting used to his glasses. He has shaved his beard and still wears the same jacket, so the new feature is his glasses.
questions.evidence: I see you have to wear glasses now as well. I’m still not really used to mine.

questions.prompt: You will hear two colleagues talking about a meeting. How does the woman feel about it?
questions.explanation: She expects the meeting to be cancelled because John is ill. Her reaction to hearing that it will continue shows her surprise.
questions.evidence: I can’t believe that. Without John? Oh well, I’m ready for it

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time.

questions.prompt: Songs from musicals: Susan ________.
questions.explanation: The teacher of songs from musicals is Susan Brokley. The speaker spells her surname B-R-O-K-L-E-Y.
questions.evidence: And Susan Brokley will teach you to sing songs from famous musicals. Her surname’s spelt B-R-O-K-L-E-Y.

questions.prompt: When: Friday, at ________ p.m.
questions.explanation: The concert begins at half past eight. Eight o’clock is only the time when the theatre doors open.
questions.evidence: It’ll begin at half past eight

questions.prompt: Colour of clothes: ________.
questions.explanation: Performers are asked to wear blue so that they look similar. Black is mentioned as the traditional concert colour, but it is not required here.
questions.evidence: we ask that they’re blue so everyone looks similar.

questions.prompt: Map of building: available from the ________.
questions.explanation: The speaker says a map showing the rooms is available from the receptionist. Teachers and the security guard can give directions, but they are not the source of the map.
questions.evidence: There’s also a map showing where all the rooms are, which you can get from the receptionist.

questions.prompt: Lunch: eat in the ________.
questions.explanation: Students should take their food to the hall. The kitchen is for preparing food and has nowhere to sit and eat.
questions.evidence: take your sandwiches or whatever to the hall

questions.prompt: Car park: costs £________ per day.
questions.explanation: The daily parking charge is £3. The £20 price is for a monthly pass, while £15 is the total for the week.
questions.evidence: it’s cheaper to pay daily, which is £3

parts.context: You will hear a man giving information to people who are starting a one-week singing course.
parts.heading: One-week singing course

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Why did Mickey decide to become a hairdresser?
questions.explanation: After college, a friend offered him work in his hairdressing shop. Mickey accepted and stayed, rather than deliberately following his parents’ career.
questions.evidence: a friend said I could help in his hairdresser’s shop, so I did, and I ended up staying!

questions.prompt: On a typical day at work, Mickey says that he
questions.explanation: He thinks it is best to mix up the work, including different cuts and colouring. He makes time for breaks and does not mind staying late.
questions.evidence: it’s best if we mix things up — do a few women’s cuts, some mens, some colour.

questions.prompt: The part of the job which Mickey likes most is
questions.explanation: He most enjoys exchanging news with customers who return regularly. He is less keen on inventing new styles for them.
questions.evidence: I really enjoy exchanging news with the people who come back regularly for haircuts.

questions.prompt: What part of his job does Mickey dislike?
questions.explanation: He finds the required health and safety courses extremely dull. Rude customers do not bother him, and he is willing to share his knowledge.
questions.evidence: We have to take health and safety courses which I find extremely dull

questions.prompt: How does Mickey feel after cutting a customer’s hair?
questions.explanation: He usually thinks he could do something better and keeps trying to improve. This shows that he wants to continue learning.
questions.evidence: I usually feel there’s something I could do better, so I’m always trying to improve

questions.prompt: Mickey recommends that people who want to work as hairdressers
questions.explanation: He warns that people often mistakenly think they have learned everything. His advice is to keep learning rather than assume they know it all.
questions.evidence: a lot of people make the mistake of thinking they’ve learned all there is to learn — that’s rarely true.

parts.context: You will hear an interview with a man called Mickey Diaz, who is talking about his work as a hairdresser.

parts.title: Part 1
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: What has the man forgotten to pack for the trip?
questions.explanation: He realises he has left his torch behind. He remembered his sleeping bag this time and already has his walking boots.
questions.evidence: I’ve just realised I’ve left my torch behind.

questions.prompt: What time is the plane expected to depart?
questions.explanation: The flight has been delayed and is not expected to take off until 12.15. The other times refer to the original departure and the check-in deadline.
questions.evidence: this flight is delayed and is unlikely to take off until 12.15.

questions.prompt: Where did the family go at the weekend?
questions.explanation: They bought discounted tickets to visit a castle. The theatre was an earlier idea, and the art gallery was a previous family outing.
questions.evidence: We ended up getting some discount tickets to visit a castle.

questions.prompt: What are the man and woman going to order?
questions.explanation: They finally agree to ask for a jug of tap water after noticing the prices. They do not choose bottled water or separate glasses of still and sparkling water.
questions.evidence: What about asking for a jug of tap water — it tastes just as good.
questions.cueEndQuote: Especially if they put ice and lemon in it. Good idea.

questions.prompt: Which photograph did the man take?
questions.explanation: The man is interested in water, particularly scenes showing rain, and points out one of his own photographs. The desert and lake photographs were taken by other people.
questions.evidence: I’m interested in water, especially scenes showing rain. Have a look at this one of mine.

questions.prompt: How does the man suggest his friends should travel to the concert?
questions.explanation: He suggests taking the underground to Greenoaks and walking from the station. A taxi is suggested only for the journey home.
questions.evidence: You could always take the underground to Greenoaks station and it’s only a short walk from there.

questions.prompt: What is the weather forecast for the north this morning?
questions.explanation: Heavy snow showers are forecast in northern areas this morning. The fog is in the south, while stronger winds are expected in the evening.
questions.evidence: There’ll be heavy snow showers, mainly in northern areas

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: You will hear a boy telling a friend about plans for his birthday. How does he feel about the plans he’s made?
questions.explanation: He wants to invite both his college friends and football teammates, but a cycling group that large would be unsuitable. He is disappointed about having to choose between them.
questions.evidence: I’ll have to choose between them, which is a shame.
questions.cueStartQuote: it wouldn’t be a good idea to have so many people riding together

questions.prompt: You will hear two friends talking about a football match they went to. They both think that
questions.explanation: The woman notices that fewer people attended than usual, and the man suggests the cold weather caused the low attendance. They disagree about how enjoyable the match and the referee were.
questions.evidence: there weren’t nearly as many people watching as there normally are.
questions.cueEndQuote: The cold weather might be the reason for the low numbers.

questions.prompt: You will hear a man telling his friend about a skiing holiday. How did he feel during the holiday?
questions.explanation: He struggled with an advanced route and had to give up. His friends laughed, which made him feel silly and embarrassed about his skiing.
questions.evidence: The others all found this very funny, which made me feel pretty silly.

questions.prompt: You will hear two friends talking about cars. The woman thinks the best way to get information about new cars is from
questions.explanation: She prefers reading online opinions from people who own the cars. She trusts these owners more than advertisements or television information.
questions.evidence: I’d always rather see what car owners say than trust adverts or stuff on TV.
questions.cueStartQuote: some useful places to look online where people who’ve bought new cars give their opinions

questions.prompt: You will hear a woman telling a friend about a singing competition. What does the woman say about it?
questions.explanation: Organising the competition is taking up a great deal of her time, including most evenings. She is not judging it and prefers watching to performing.
questions.evidence: I’m spending ages sorting things out, including most evenings.

questions.prompt: You will hear a woman talking to a friend about her recent move to a city. How does the woman feel about it?
questions.explanation: Having everything nearby means she walks everywhere and is fitter than when she lived in the countryside. This health benefit was unexpected.
questions.evidence: I’m actually fitter than when I lived in the countryside. I hadn’t expected that.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time.

questions.prompt: Kelly did a degree in ________ at university.
questions.explanation: Although she now knows a lot about computing, Kelly says that her university degree was in art.
questions.evidence: I actually studied art for my degree.

questions.prompt: Kelly really enjoys going to work because of the ________ at the company.
questions.explanation: She praises the software but says it is the people who make the company such a good workplace.
questions.evidence: it’s the people there that make it such a fantastic place to work.

questions.prompt: Kelly’s department is responsible for creating ________ in cartoons.
questions.explanation: Her own department works on the animals in each story. Other departments create the human characters and buildings.
questions.evidence: the one I’m in works on animals in the story

questions.prompt: At the moment Kelly is trying to develop her ________ skills.
questions.explanation: Kelly has just started acting classes to improve her understanding of filmmaking. Her writing course took place last year.
questions.evidence: I’ve just started doing acting classes, which are surprisingly useful for understanding filmmaking

questions.prompt: It takes Kelly’s company ________ to make a full-length cartoon film.
questions.explanation: Her company uses computers and takes eight months to make a full-length film. The two-year timescale refers to the traditional method using individual drawings.
questions.evidence: Compare that to the eight months it takes my company to do the same

questions.prompt: Kelly’s next project will be some cartoons for a ________.
questions.explanation: She says her next project is something for a website. It will be a new challenge after her work on children’s comedy films.
questions.evidence: It’s actually something for a website.

parts.context: You will hear a woman called Kelly Robinson talking about her work as a maker of cartoon films.
parts.heading: The maker of cartoon films

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Rosie swam a lot when she was very young because
questions.explanation: Her brother Joel was a very good swimmer, so she practised frequently to become as fast as him. Matching her brother motivated her.
questions.evidence: Joel was better at swimming than anyone we knew, and I practised as often as possible so I could swim as fast as him.

questions.prompt: What did Rosie dislike about doing serious swimming training?
questions.explanation: Training and competitions sometimes made her miss school, which upset her. She enjoyed chatting during the journey and still saw her friends when she could.
questions.evidence: I couldn’t attend school sometimes, which I was unhappy about.

questions.prompt: When Rosie won the Swim Stars International competition she was
questions.explanation: She had trained hard and expected to do well. What surprised her was that people wanted to read and watch interviews with her.
questions.evidence: I couldn’t believe people wanted to read and watch interviews with me!

questions.prompt: Rosie says she needs more help with the cost of
questions.explanation: A sportswear company already pays for flights and supplies branded equipment. Her parents still pay a lot for hotels, so she wants support with accommodation.
questions.evidence: It’d be great if they also gave me financial support for hotels

questions.prompt: What has Rosie changed since she got a new coach?
questions.explanation: Her new coach has changed how she moves her arms through the water, improving her speed. Her fitness routine and diet have remained the same.
questions.evidence: thanks to her suggestions about the way I move my arms through the water, I’ve already seen improvements

questions.prompt: What is Rosie planning to do in Spain?
questions.explanation: She will attend a summer training course with swimmers she has not met before. She will not be racing there, and her short break comes first.
questions.evidence: I’ll work with lots of swimmers I haven’t met before.

parts.context: You will hear an interview with a girl called Rosie Banks, who swims in international competitions.
